family's `source` as path:line — never permalinks (D34: a pre-commit renderer cannot know the
SHA of the commit it is creating).
The landing build consumes this file as pinned data and stamps `url`, `verified-at: <pinned
framework sha>` and resolved permalinks at build time (D42 falsifier (b): a URL-dependent
value is a landing-side stamp, not a face fact). The landing runs no framework script (D35).
Fence-region checking on the face pages (FS1 page arm) activates at S1 when the pages land
(D24b byte-identity seam); today the check is this manifest's own byte-identity.

rules.label: beta
rules.definition: One-command install; a rule provably fires on your code (`npm run lint` goes RED on a planted violation); rule docs are generated from the delivered rule set.
rules.caveat: Two runtime rules (R7/R8) ship deferred behind AIF_STRICT_RUNTIME=1 — a default lint run stays green on their triggers.

factory.label: experimental
factory.definition: Stack scaffold + templates; a dedicated rule-pack is not yet shipped.
factory.caveat: The factory depth clones a preset whose rule-packs are uneven — the per-stack rows govern.

ts-server.label: beta
ts-server.definition: One-command install; a rule provably fires on your code (`npm run lint` goes RED on a planted violation); rule docs are generated from the delivered rule set.
ts-server.caveat: Default TS lane; it shares the manifest-rendered multi-stack rule pack with react-next — no ts-server-specific rules beyond it.

react-next.label: beta
react-next.definition: One-command install; a rule provably fires on your code (`npm run lint` goes RED on a planted violation); rule docs are generated from the delivered rule set.
react-next.caveat: Wires three custom rules by default (two more behind AIF_STRICT_RUNTIME=1) on top of the shared manifest-rendered rule pack.

react-spa.label: early
react-spa.definition: Installs one-command and wires real rules, but the rule-pack is still growing.
react-spa.caveat: Wires two custom rules by default (two more behind AIF_STRICT_RUNTIME=1); the rule-pack is still growing.

react-native.label: experimental
react-native.definition: Stack scaffold + templates; a dedicated rule-pack is not yet shipped.
react-native.caveat: Ships stack scaffold + templates; no custom rule is wired yet.

python.label: alpha
python.definition: Installs one-command and fires on verified fixtures; rule generation is partial or deferred.
python.caveat: Non-npm lane — ast-grep + ruff only; the npm custom-rule engine does not apply.

cargo.label: alpha
cargo.definition: Installs one-command and fires on verified fixtures; rule generation is partial or deferred.
cargo.caveat: cargo-deny ships as a starter config no workflow runs; the clippy bans are the enforced lane (CI-failing when violated).

go.label: alpha
go.definition: Installs one-command and fires on verified fixtures; rule generation is partial or deferred.
go.caveat: The forbidigo ban ships as .golangci.yml on a fresh repo, or as getff-golangci.yml when you already have one (inert locally until you opt in); the delivered CI workflow runs it build-failing in both cells; rule generation is deferred (operator, 2026-09-09).

core.goal: install -> a rule provably fires on your code
core.profileFlag: --profile core (core is never the default — install.sh:648 makes the non-interactive default `env`)

steps.title: Install at core depth
steps.action: On npm stack layers: From your project root run `bash <getff>/setup -y --profile core <stack>` — `core` must be named, because `-y` on its own resolves to `env` (install.sh:648). (stacks: ts-server, react-next, react-spa, react-native; `python`, `cargo` and `go` are separate non-npm toolchain lanes, each an explicit positional — `./setup cargo` or `bash install.sh cargo`, the wrapper forwards lanes verbatim). Omit the stack to auto-detect.

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: On npm stack layers: `ls AGENTS.md .ai-factory/ scripts/` — you should see AGENTS.md, `.ai-factory/{DESCRIPTION.md,ARCHITECTURE.md,RULES.md}` and `scripts/audit-ai-docs.sh`. These payload requirements apply to npm stacks; toolchain lanes use their native payload lists. Toolchain lanes follow toolchainLanes verification (AI Usage Guide §2.4); cargo/Go install no passport or skills.

steps.title: Fill the project passport
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` in `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md` (domain, stack, constraints, non-goals). This is the file AGENTS.md sends every future session to first, so a passport left unfilled degrades every later session. Toolchain lanes follow toolchainLanes verification (AI Usage Guide §2.4); cargo/Go install no passport or skills.

steps.title: Prove the rules are not inert on your layout
steps.action: On npm stack layers: `bash scripts/check-rule-globs.sh` — fails when a shipped custom rule matches ZERO files in your layout, i.e. it is installed but silently enforcing nothing. If it fires, widen `RULE_GLOBS` in `eslint.config.mjs` to cover your layout. On a brand-new skeleton with no source files yet this FAILS by design — every rule matches zero files. That is the expected first run; re-run it once your first `src/` files exist. Toolchain lanes follow toolchainLanes verification (AI Usage Guide §2.4); cargo/Go install no passport or skills.
steps.evidence: scripts/check-rule-globs.sh (shipped at core; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

steps.title: Watch a rule actually fire
steps.action: On npm stack layers: `bash scripts/check-fences-fire.sh` — plants deliberately-bad input in a temp dir and asserts the installed ESLint rules go RED on it. This is the first-rule-fires moment: an installed rule that has never been seen to fire is an unproven claim. Toolchain lanes follow toolchainLanes verification (AI Usage Guide §2.4); cargo/Go install no passport or skills.

steps.title: Fire a rule on YOUR code, not a fixture
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Plant one violation of a shipped getff rule in YOUR tree and run your stack's native gate — the RED line names your file. npm: add `z.string().parse(input)` to a file under a boundary glob (`**/routes/**`, `**/handlers/**`, `**/controllers/**`, `**/app/api/**`, `**/actions/**`), run `npm run lint` — RED from `rules-as-tests/no-unsafe-zod-parse` (R2, the one custom rule wired unconditionally; R7/R8 fire only under `AIF_STRICT_RUNTIME=1`).
steps.evidence: templates/ts-server/eslint.config.mjs:180 (R2 unconditional); setup.d/70-deps.sh:75 (npm run lint); setup.d/45-python.sh:587 / 46-cargo.sh:256 / 47-go.sh:252 (lane firing self-checks)

steps.title: Run the gate you will run every day
steps.action: On npm stack layers: `bash scripts/audit-ai-docs.sh` — drift + code-vs-docs probes (~10 sec). Expect findings on a fresh project; the INSTALL-FOR-AI «Expected first-run failures» table lists which ones are normal. Toolchain lanes follow toolchainLanes verification (AI Usage Guide §2.4); cargo/Go install no passport or skills.

steps.title: Continue into rule research in the same session
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Invoke `/rule-research` (or read `.claude/agents/rule-researcher.md` on a harness without skills). The installer delivered a curated starter set; researching stack-specific rules from live documentation is the next step of the same lifecycle, not a later project. Toolchain lanes follow toolchainLanes verification (AI Usage Guide §2.4); cargo/Go install no passport or skills.

steps.title: Install at env depth
steps.action: On an npm layer, re-run `bash <getff>/install.sh <stack> --profile env`, or explicitly opt in with `--refresh --profile env`. Bare --refresh preserves existing depth. Toolchain lanes use native verification instead of the npm skill roster.

steps.title: Read the tier + degradation SSOT
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Open `.ai-factory/tier-home.md`. It owns the Tier 0/1/2 routing criteria and the capability-absence degradation matrix — what still works when there is no aif runtime, no executor-tier model, or a non-Claude-Code harness. AGENTS.md only points here; the criteria live in this one file.

steps.title: Take one idea through `/arch`
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Invoke `/arch <topic>` — the external design contour turns a raw idea into a reviewed design plus a routed handoff. On a harness without skills, read `.claude/skills/arch/SKILL.md` and follow it by hand.

steps.title: Read the tier + degradation SSOT
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Open `.ai-factory/tier-home.md` — it decides which tier a task routes to, and what degrades when a capability is absent.

steps.title: Write your first kickoff
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Create `.ai-factory/orchestrator-prompts/<work-item>/kickoff.md`: a `Type:` line (`fix` / `research` / `feature`), the goal, and — if the work splits into parallel sub-steps — a `## §1 Sub-wave` section with one table row per sub-step.

steps.title: Ask the pipeline what to start next
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Invoke `/pipeline`. It reads your kickoffs plus `.ai-factory/orchestrator-prompts/plan.md` (created on first run), ranks them, and emits a launch table. An empty backlog reports «nothing queued» — that is normal, not an error.
steps.evidence: .claude/skills/pipeline/SKILL.md (shipped at env+; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

steps.title: Dispatch the top row and read the result
steps.action: On npm stack layers: Dispatch the launch table's top row, then bring the finished branch back with `/harvest`. If a task stalls or the runtime misbehaves, `/aif-doctor` is the diagnostic entry point.
